families.title: LLNet: An Intent-Driven Approach to Instructing Softwarized Network Devices Using a Small Language Model
families.workflow: Intent JSON to confirmed switch rules
families.path: Intent handler; SDN/device manager. Request-driven JSON interpretation, user confirmation, and rule deployment on softwarized switches.

checks.Feasibility: Network Manager detects conflicts with installed intents.
checks.Candidate coverage: Intent Converter checks named devices and supported scenario types.

families.note: Human confirmation and syntax checks precede deployment.

families.title: Evaluating Agentic Configuration Repair for Computer Networks
families.path: Configuration-repair assistant. Offline iterative edits and diagnosis over Cornetto configurations; forwarding properties are simulated.

checks.Feasibility: Batfish/Config2Spec verification, used either only for final scoring or also as agent feedback depending on the condition.

families.note: Verification evaluates the final configuration in all conditions and guides intermediate repairs only in the feedback condition.

families.title: Don't Mind the Gap: Bridging Network-Wide Objectives and Device-Level Configurations
families.path: Routing-policy compiler. Operator policies compile into device-level BGP configurations.

checks.Feasibility: Propane compiler computes topology-constrained permitted paths and compiles routing preferences.

families.title: Intent-Based Infrastructure and Service Orchestration Using Agentic-AI
families.path: Intent handler; infrastructure/service orchestrator. Agent plan and dispatch, Kubernetes cluster/resource changes, and network-service deployment.
families.note: The workflow uses cluster-state feedback and human approval for sensitive tools.

families.title: Software-Defined Network Assimilation: Bridging the Last Mile towards Centralized Network Configuration Management with NAssim
families.path: Device-model preparation and configuration mapping. Offline manual parsing, CLI/model validation, and top-k vendor-to-unified parameter mapping.

checks.Feasibility: NAssim Validator checks CLI syntax and hierarchy and tests snippets against device/configuration evidence.

families.note: Parameter top-k recommendation is selection; validation concerns device-model consistency.

families.title: Towards End-to-End Network Intent Management with Large Language Models
families.workflow: Business intent to RAN/core service configuration
families.path: Business/service intent handler. Natural-language demand becomes CFS, then RAN/core RFS configuration; translation is the measured boundary.
families.note: Resolver verification is architectural; evaluation measures translation.

families.title: Intent Assurance Using LLMs Guided by Intent Drift
families.path: Intent handler; assurance orchestrator. Intent/KPI extraction followed by collection-service fulfillment and drift-triggered repair.

checks.Feasibility: A separate LLM validator inspects the generated policy tree for omissions, ordering and attributes.

families.note: Health/drift feedback triggers assurance and repair.

families.title: Network-Wide Configuration Synthesis
families.path: Network configuration synthesizer. Datalog/SMT synthesis of OSPF, BGP, and static forwarding configurations.

checks.Feasibility: SyNET encodes specified forwarding requirements and protocol interactions into solver constraints.
checks.Candidate coverage: The synthesis contract returns a satisfying network configuration if one exists, within its formal input model.

families.title: NetComplete: Practical Network-Wide Configuration Synthesis with Autocompletion
families.path: Network configuration synthesizer. OSPF, BGP, and static-route sketch completion; synthesis runtimes are distinct from activation.

checks.Feasibility: NetComplete solves symbolic sketch constraints and checks BGP announcement-preference consistency.

families.note: Feasibility is conditional on the operator sketch and modeled routing requirements.

families.title: NetIntent: Leveraging Large Language Models for End-to-End Intent-Based SDN Automation
families.workflow: Flow generation, installation and drift repair
families.path: Intent handler; SDN controller. Flow JSON generation, LLM conflict detection, deterministic resolution/installation, and drift repair.

checks.Feasibility: LLM compares new and installed flow rules; controller policy resolves conflicts or escalates. Structural validation is a separate non-LLM component.

families.note: The workflow escalates untranslatable outputs.

families.title: Intent Engine: Natural-Language Intent Translation for Intent-Driven Orchestration in the Compute Continuum
families.path: Intent handler above compute-continuum orchestrator. State-grounded SLO construction.
families.note: Deterministic snapshot encoding, periodic monitoring and schema checks support SLO construction.

families.title: Hey, Lumi! Using Natural Language for Intent-Based Network Management
families.path: Intent handler; SDN compiler/controller. NER/assembly and user-confirmed Nile, Merlin compilation/deployment, plus a separate exploratory contradiction classifier.

checks.Feasibility: Random Forest flags intent-pair contradictions in the reported exploratory task; formal policy verification is prospective.

families.note: The exploratory contradiction classifier is evaluated in Sec. 10.1.

families.title: ITBench: Evaluating AI Agents across Diverse Real-World IT Automation Tasks
families.workflow: Network-fault diagnosis and mitigation in ITBench
families.path: SRE/assurance agent. Network-fault root-cause reports and mitigation actions in the ITBench SRE environment.
families.note: Reported aggregate timing covers the full SRE task set; network-fault tasks form a subset.

families.title: JAUNT: Joint Alignment of User Intent and Network State for QoE-Centric LLM Tool Routing
families.workflow: Per-request tool selection with latency prediction
families.path: Service/tool router. Per-request MCP tool selection combines semantic matching, a user profile, and predicted network latency.
families.note: EWMA latency predictions and candidate retrieval feed the selector.

families.title: Fast Intent-Driven Service Orchestration with Jev for 6G Edge Networks
families.workflow: Versioned intent contracts to edge placement
families.path: Intent handler; edge service scheduler. Versioned contract activation and numerical placement; modeled NR access and modeled/real OCR service paths remain distinct.

checks.Observation state: Controller versions contracts and cache identity; numerical scheduler reads current queues/capacity after interpretation.
checks.Feasibility: Shared execution layer checks placement permissions; numerical scheduler scores permitted placements under current state.

families.note: This classification describes the 6G version included in the review corpus. The RIC experiments analyzed in Sec. VII come from a subsequent code and data release. Observation handling here covers state reads and versioning.

families.title: Replacing Large Language Models with Jev Decision Models for Low-Latency Edge Service Orchestration
families.path: Intent handler; admission controller and edge scheduler. Four-field interpretation followed by shared admission and modeled or real two-node OCR execution.

checks.Observation state: Scheduler reads worker/queue state after interpretation; interpretation reuse is keyed by request text and extraction policy.
checks.Feasibility: Scheduler filters by service, placement, queue capacity, and predicted deadline; observed completion can still fail after admission.
checks.Candidate coverage: Scheduler rejects when no eligible node has a predicted completion within the deadline.

families.title: Towards Intent-Based Network Management: Large Language Models for Intent Extraction in 5G Core Networks
families.path: Core-network intent handler (functional placement). Six-class multi-label intent extraction with explanations; activation is future work.
families.note: The evaluation measures intent extraction; core-network placement is architectural.

families.title: Advanced LLM-Enhanced Intent-Based 5G Network Management using Dynamic Semantic Routes
families.workflow: Static route selection and dynamic parameters
families.path: Core-network intent router/handler. Encoder-based static routing and generated dynamic-route parameters; early and expanded report scopes are retained.
families.note: The router includes None among its semantic route options.

families.title: NLP Powered Intent Based Network Management for Private 5G Networks
families.path: Intent handler; private-5G slice/NFV orchestrator. Registered workflow/model matching leads to slice configuration, LoS classification, or NS/VIM service instantiation.
families.note: Matching selects a registered operation/model; its workflow specifies the execution actions and parameters.

families.title: Chat-Driven Optimal Management for Virtual Network Services
families.path: Intent handler; virtual-network optimizer. Chat parameters drive ILP placement/routing and an explicit accepted-request-subset decision.

checks.Feasibility: ILP enforces link, compute, latency, and placement constraints parameterized by interpreted intent.
checks.Candidate coverage: Optimizer arbitrates an acceptable request subset under joint resource constraints in the expanded report.

families.note: BERT/SVM labels and generated Llama JSON are alternative interpreters supplying parameters to the solver.

families.title: What Do LLMs Need to Synthesize Correct Router Configurations?
families.path: Router-configuration translator/synthesizer. Cross-vendor translation and multi-router BGP policy generation, refined with verification feedback.

checks.Feasibility: Campion checks configuration equivalence; Batfish checks the scoped routing policy. Syntax and semantic feedback are iterated separately.

families.note: Campion and Batfish verify modeled routing/forwarding behavior.

families.title: LLM-Based AI Agent for Virtual Network Function Deployment
families.path: VNF deployment orchestrator. MOP-to-Python/Ansible workflow generation and iterative repair in a network digital twin.
families.note: Digital-twin execution tests generated workflows and returns logs for iterative repair; validation covers those executions.

families.title: Toward Intent-Based Network Automation for Smart Environments: A Healthcare 4.0 Use Case
families.workflow: Intent entity extraction; proposed SDN activation
families.path: Intent handler above SDN (proposed placement). BERT extracts user, goal, action, target, and time-frame entities; SDN activation/assurance remains architectural.
families.note: Token labels extract open entity values.

families.title: Practical Intent-Driven Routing Configuration Synthesis
families.path: Routing-policy compiler and activation controller. Aura compiles per-switch BGP policies, stages configurations, and changes active routing policy after convergence checks.

checks.Feasibility: Routing-policy validation uses container-based switch emulation before deployment.

families.note: Compilation, operator review, deployment, and convergence are distinct boundaries.

families.title: Snowcap: Synthesizing Network-Wide Configuration Updates
families.workflow: Safe update ordering with convergence waits
families.path: Configuration-update planner/controller. Snowcap synthesizes an ordered update plan, then applies commands with convergence waits.

checks.Feasibility: LTL safety requirements constrain every intermediate update state; a forwarding supergraph overapproximates convergence states.

families.note: The computed update order enforces safety across intermediate states.

families.title: Safely and Automatically Updating In-Network ACL Configurations with Intent Language
families.path: ACL verification and update controller. Jinjing checks, repairs, migrates, or generates ACL updates under scoped reachability intent.

checks.Feasibility: ACL reachability predicates and placement constraints are checked/solved with formal constraints and SMT.

families.title: FaulT-Bench: Towards Benchmarking Network Troubleshooting LLM Agents under Unreliable User Tickets
families.path: Network diagnostic assistant. Agents inspect a live emulated network, return diagnosis, and propose remediation under unreliable user tickets.

checks.Observation state: The diagnostic agent is tasked with checking ticket premises against tool-observed network state; false-premise and wrong-device tickets test this responsibility.

families.note: Evaluation tests the agent's premise checks, diagnoses and proposed fixes.

families.title: Intent-Based Network Configuration Using Large Language Models
families.workflow: Confirmed intent translation to NFV deployment
families.path: Intent handler; NFV orchestrator. VNF/SFC or formal-policy JSON translation, human confirmation, and NI-NFVO deployment.

checks.Feasibility: NFV-Intent and NI-MANO check infrastructure-supported resource flavors and user capability before deployment.

families.note: Verification ownership is task-specific; the early and expanded translation datasets remain separate evidence scopes.

families.title: NetConfEval: Can LLMs Facilitate Network Configuration?
families.workflow: Task-specific policy, API and routing generation
families.path: Intent/configuration handler; routing-program assistant. JSON/Datalog policies, API calls with arguments, routing code, FRR/RIFT/P4 configuration, and a scoped live BGP change.

checks.Feasibility: LLM conflict diagnosis is one scoped output; syntax/tests and network verifiers provide task-specific feedback. Operator confirmation remains needed for language-to-intent correctness.

families.note: API calls construct arguments as well as selecting a function name. Evaluation and activation boundaries vary across benchmark tasks.

families.title: A Network Arena for Benchmarking AI Agents on Network Troubleshooting
families.path: Network diagnostic assistant. NIKA uses tool-driven network observation for anomaly detection, localization, and root-cause reports.
families.note: Mitigation safety and execution are explicitly future work. The early four-switch demonstration and expanded benchmark remain separate scopes.

families.title: INTA: Intent-Based Translation for Network Configuration with LLM Agents
families.path: Cross-vendor configuration translator. INTA combines manual retrieval, target-CLI generation, syntax correction, and a semantic-consistency report.

checks.Feasibility: Command-tree matching checks syntax/view structure; an LLM checks source-target semantic equivalence and refines disagreements.

families.note: The LLM judges source-target semantic consistency.

families.title: NetLLM: Adapting Large Language Models for Networking
families.path: Application/networking controller; cluster scheduler. A learned networking head selects video bitrate or a scheduling stage and executor count.
families.note: The decision interfaces cover bitrate and scheduling actions. Prediction, training, and aggregate performance measurements have separate evaluation scopes.

families.title: NetArena: Dynamic Benchmarks for AI Agents in Network Automation
families.path: Network planning and repair agent. NetArena agents modify topology plans, emulated routing configuration, or Kubernetes network policies.
families.note: Environment-grounded evaluation provides feedback on agent actions. The review consolidates the NetPress alias under this family.

families.title: OmniPlan: An Adaptive Framework for Timely and Near-Optimal Network Planning Optimization
families.path: Intent handler; network-planning optimizer. Preference extraction and expert selection feed weight adaptation and device-placement/link-routing optimization.

checks.Feasibility: MIP experts compile explicit planning constraints; fast experts use scoped resource-constrained heuristics.

families.note: Learned weight adaptation constructs continuous values. Semantic validation is proposed future work.

families.title: OSDF: An Intent-based Software Defined Network Programming Framework
families.workflow: Policies to SDN paths and conflict advice
families.path: Intent-based SDN controller. OSDF maps policies to paths/meters and computes conflict classifications and repair recommendations.

checks.Feasibility: Policy conflict module applies explicit rules for redundancy, shadowing, generalization, correlation, and overlap; recommendations go to the administrator.

families.title: VIVoNet: Visually-represented, Intent-based, Voice-assisted Networking
families.workflow: Confirmed voice intent to OpenFlow rules
families.path: Voice intent handler; SDN controller. Alexa extracts operation/endpoints and confirms intent; deterministic path computation installs OpenFlow rules.
families.note: Successful rule push marks the activation acknowledgement.

families.title: GP4P4: Enabling Self-Programming Networks
families.path: Programmable-data-plane synthesizer. Genetic search constructs P4 programs against packet-behavior rules.

checks.Feasibility: Program fitness evaluates the specified behavioral examples/rules during search.

families.note: Search stops on a valid program or at the generation limit.

families.title: Refining Network Intents for Self-Driving Networks
families.workflow: Confirmed intent to NFV service-chain deployment
families.path: Intent handler; NFV service-chain deployer. Entity extraction and seq2seq Nile generation precede user confirmation and SONATA-NFV deployment.

checks.Feasibility: Intent Deployer asserts consistency with existing network configuration and warns the operator before deployment.

families.title: The Role of Intent-Based Networking in ICT Supply Chains
families.path: Supply-chain access-policy handler (conceptual). Controlled language is parsed with regex/vocabulary rules and refined using organizational access policies.

checks.Feasibility: Proposed policy configurator resolves authorization conflicts using organizational scope/hierarchy before calling the controller.

families.note: The paper presents conceptual examples.

families.title: Intent-based Network Management and Orchestration for Smart Distribution Grids
families.workflow: Conceptual smart-grid intent to network slices
families.path: Intent/service orchestrator; slice MANO (conceptual). Smart-grid intent and SLA become a service request, GST/NEST profile, and proposed network-slice resource configuration.

checks.Feasibility: The proposed architecture assigns SLA validation and profile trade-off checks to intent/service orchestration.

families.note: Functional transformations are specified without enough implementation detail to choose one decision-interface class.

families.title: Mission-Critical Public Safety Networking: An Intent-Driven Service Orchestration Perspective
families.workflow: Controlled intent to simulated public-safety service
families.path: Intent handler; public-safety service orchestrator. Controlled-language processing maps requests to LTE/PTT service templates, followed by ns-3 access and voice-service execution.

checks.Feasibility: The architecture assigns resource, subscription, and conflict checks to intent validation using telemetry, with user dialogue on failure.

families.note: The paper reports an architectural validation design and simulated service outcomes.

families.title: Experimental Demonstration of Partially Disaggregated Optical Network Control Using the Physical Layer Digital Twin
families.path: Optical path computation and SDN controller. Digital-twin optical tuning and modulation feasibility feed route/spectrum assignment and ONOS/NETCONF lightpath deployment.

checks.Feasibility: L-PCE and RSA restrict modulation/path/channel combinations by optical feasibility and wavelength continuity.

families.note: Optical feasibility and post-configuration transmission checks are tied to the measured photonics setup.

families.title: Knowledge-based Intent Modeling for Next Generation Cellular Networks
families.path: Knowledge-based intent handler; service orchestrator. KG queries form service/network intent; ns-3 deployment and KPI-threshold compliance reporting follow.

checks.Feasibility: Network-layer validation compares resource requirements with available resources and service models before orchestration.

families.title: Grooming Connectivity Intents in IP-Optical Networks Using Directed Acyclic Graphs
families.path: IP-optical intent compiler/orchestrator. Graph algorithms groom connectivity intents into shared path/modulation/spectrum resources.
families.note: SAP/JML/LDJML are alternative algorithms for the same compilation responsibility; the reported evaluation is simulation.

families.title: An Intent-based Framework for Vehicular Edge Computing
families.path: Vehicular-edge intent orchestrator. Declarative requests are mapped to constrained nodes/links, then installed or reconfigured using ONOS/Mininet.

checks.Feasibility: PAI/LAM heuristics map CPU, memory, location, bandwidth, latency and priority constraints in the request/network models.

families.title: Wireless Multi-Agent Generative AI: From Connected Intelligence to Collective Intelligence
families.path: Distributed wireless power controller. GPT-4 agents propose transmit powers using prior-round actions in a four-user power-game case.
families.note: The four-user case evaluates constructed transmit-power actions.

families.title: Direct-Conflict Resolution in Intent-Driven Autonomous Networks
families.path: RAN intent-conflict resolver. Bargaining methods choose antenna tilt to reconcile coverage/capacity utility in an ns-3 LTE scenario.

checks.Feasibility: Explicit feasible utility sets and bargaining/Jain-fairness selection resolve the modeled two-intent parameter conflict.

families.note: Bargaining resolves the modeled coverage/capacity utility conflict.

families.title: Intent Profiling and Translation Through Emergent Communication
families.path: Device intent encoder; network slice allocator. MAPPO maps device intent to discrete symbols and then maps messages to QoS slices.
families.note: Constraints are specified in the optimization problem.

families.title: PreConfig: A Pretrained Model for Automating Network Configuration
families.path: Device-configuration assistant. PreConfig generates configurations/commands, translates vendors, and explains device configuration semantics.
families.note: Evaluation concerns configuration artifacts and their explanations.

families.title: Predictive Intent Maintenance with Intent Drift Detection in Next Generation Network
families.path: Intent-assurance monitor. Predictive models and a greedy comparator flag intent drift from monitored throughput time series.
families.note: The monitor detects KPI drift in throughput time series.

families.title: Knowledge Graph Embedding in Intent-Based Networking
families.path: Knowledge-based intent handler. Entity extraction and KG completion form intent templates; a learned triple classifier outputs validity.

checks.Feasibility: KG2E performs learned plausibility classification of each intent triple as valid/invalid.

families.title: LLM-Based Intent Processing and Network Optimization Using Attention-Based Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
families.workflow: Intent validity to hierarchical RAN control
families.path: Intent handler; hierarchical RAN controller. KPI extraction and validity checks drive application selection, traffic steering, sleep, beam, power, and handover policies.

checks.Feasibility: Traffic prediction and explicit QoS-drift thresholds determine intent validity before hierarchical control.

families.note: The validity rule uses QoS drift; the reported system result jointly covers the selected applications.

families.title: Online Learning for Autonomous Management of Intent-based 6G Networks
families.workflow: Parent-bandit selection of joint service priorities
families.path: Intent-conflict resolver. A parent bandit combines service-agent predictions into joint service-priority choices.

checks.Feasibility: A learned parent-agent policy chooses among priority combinations to resolve modeled resource conflicts.

families.title: Large Language Models for Zero Touch Network Configuration Management
families.path: Intent handler; configuration orchestrator. LLM intent classification/translation feed iterative device-configuration generation with verification feedback.

checks.Feasibility: A separate Batfish verifier checks generated configuration behavior; orchestrator coordinates feedback and regeneration.

families.note: Reported time spans the whole pipeline through final generation and verification.

families.title: CAIP: Detecting Router Misconfigurations with Context-Aware Iterative Prompting of LLMs
families.path: Configuration diagnostic assistant. CAIP iteratively requests relevant configuration context and generates error reports/explanations.

checks.Feasibility: The LLM diagnoses syntax and dependency conflicts using progressively retrieved configuration context.

families.title: Poster: Could Large Language Models Perform Network Management?
families.path: Wireless-mesh management assistant. Zero-shot model recommendations select a management action for observed events in a three-node scenario.
families.note: Evaluation measures management recommendations.

families.title: End-to-End Edge AI Service Provisioning Framework in 6G ORAN
families.workflow: Intent/model selection to service and xApp creation
families.path: Intent handler; service orchestrator; PCF interaction; xApp construction. Developer-intent profiling and model recommendation lead to API-service deployment, PCF policy interaction, and a generated QoS-monitoring xApp.
families.note: The prototype uses OAI/FlexRIC components for LLM-assisted provisioning.

families.title: RAG-Enabled Intent Reasoning for Application-Network Interaction
families.workflow: Retrieved context to structured network intent
families.path: Application-network intent handler. RAG refines service scenarios and constructs structured network intent from retrieved context.
families.note: Intent validation and policy mapping are architectural components beyond the measured translation layer.

families.title: ALLSTaR: Automated LLM-Driven Scheduler Generation and Testing for Intent-Based RAN
families.workflow: Lua scheduler construction before slot execution
families.path: Scheduler construction assistant; RAN device-side scheduler/dApp. LLMs generate/review Lua schedulers; generated code performs per-slot PRB allocation and intent-composed scheduling.
families.note: LLM construction/review precedes runtime scheduling; scheduler construction uses a pre-tested component library.

families.title: Intelligent Channel Allocation for IEEE 802.11be Multi-Link Operation: When MAB Meets LLM
families.workflow: Wi-Fi channel initialization followed by search
families.path: Wi-Fi channel allocator. LLM channel initialization is followed by BAI-MCTS search over remaining station configurations.
families.note: The carrier-sensing feasibility model supports throughput evaluation.

families.title: Toward an Intent-Based and Ontology-Driven Autonomic Security Response in Security Orchestration Automation and Response
families.path: Security intent decision/enforcement agents. IDA selects persistent/transient mitigation intents; IEA maps security intent to Kubernetes filtering configuration.

checks.Candidate coverage: Ontology queries restrict candidate techniques to instantiated, operable artifacts with compatible defensive properties.

families.note: IDA planning is a design assumption; the implementation example covers low-level enforcement.

families.title: Intent-Based Network for RAN Management with Large Language Models
families.path: RAN management over O1. History analysis informs generated TxPower strategy/configuration, applied using NETCONF and assessed with performance-management data.
families.note: The prompt supplies configuration limits for O1 management.

families.title: A Novel Integrated Architecture for Intent Based Approach and Zero Touch Networks
families.workflow: Intent translation to learned throughput control
families.path: Intent handler; throughput controller. LLM/Nile translation and conflict checks feed a Q-learning traffic-shaping controller in an OAI environment.

checks.Feasibility: The intent translation component includes a basic check against previously configured intents; implementation/coverage is only briefly described.

families.title: Understanding Network Behaviors through Natural Language Question-Answering
families.workflow: Fact graph and generated network queries
families.path: Network behavior query assistant. Configuration is converted to a fact-graph representation; generated Python/Datalog queries are executed to answer network questions.
families.note: The generated query defines the network question evaluated by routing simulation.

families.title: A Secured Intent-Based Networking (sIBN) with Data-Driven Time-Aware Intrusion Detection
families.path: Intent ingress/security filter. XGBoost flags malicious or tampered intent before downstream processing.

families.title: 5G Network Automation Using Local Large Language Models and Retrieval-Augmented Generation
families.path: 5G command intent handler. Local LLM request classification selects a category; retrieved examples guide executable command generation.

families.title: Efficient Asynchronous Federated Evaluation with Strategy Similarity Awareness for Intent-Based Networking in Industrial Internet of Things
families.path: Intent translator; deployment evaluator; network controller. Structured strategy generation is followed by learned deployability approval and command mapping/deployment.

checks.Feasibility: Federated predictive evaluators estimate strategy deployability/performance before the controller installs a configuration.

families.title: Network Self-Configuration based on Fine-Tuned Small Language Models
families.path: Configuration-generation agent. Intent classification and step planning lead to iterative Cisco configuration generation and a verification report.

checks.Feasibility: The Verifier is assigned syntax, dependency and objective checks with regeneration feedback.

families.note: The verification module's implementation is unspecified. Reported time spans the whole configuration-generation pipeline.

families.title: Graph-Symbolic Policy Enforcement and Control (G-SPEC): A Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Safe Agentic AI in 5G Autonomous Networks
families.path: 5G action planner; controller admission guard. A language planner proposes actions; SHACL gates a hypothetical next-state graph before Open5GS orchestration.

checks.Observation state: A SHACL/SPARQL freshness guard rejects stale graph entities by lastUpdated age and requires refreshed telemetry.
checks.Feasibility: G-SPEC checks topology, resource, operational-state, and bounded state-change policies before execution.

families.note: Evaluation reports policy examples and tests of the graph guards.

families.title: Agentic AI Empowered Intent-Based Networking for 6G
families.path: Cross-domain slice orchestrator; RAN/core specialists. An orchestrator combines RAN band/sector and UPF recommendations into provisioning arguments.

checks.Feasibility: Specialist LLMs reason over latency/capacity; the orchestrator checks compatibility of the combined recommendation before calling the provisioning tool.

families.note: The orchestrator agent performs the consistency check.

families.title: Vision Language Models for Optimization-Driven Intent Processing in Autonomous Networks
families.path: Optimization-code assistant; SDN controller. VLMs generate Gurobi programs; a scoped example solves flows, translates them into rules, and deploys/tests with Ryu/Mininet.

checks.Feasibility: Gurobi solves the constraints encoded in the generated program.

families.note: The 85-instance program benchmark and a separate two-node executed demonstration are distinct evidence scopes.

families.title: IntAgent: NWDAF-Based Intent LLM Agent Towards Advanced Next Generation Networks
families.workflow: Planned, timed slice-rate changes via tools
families.path: NWDAF-based intent agent; core/session-management tools. An agent plans timed slice AMBR changes; tools apply and restore the settings.

checks.Feasibility: Dedicated feasibility and session-management tools evaluate action constraints and allowed QoS/state transitions before execution.

families.note: NWDAF analytics, tool planning, timed actions, and observed throughput have different timing boundaries.

families.title: LEAD-Drift: Real-time and Explainable Intent Drift Detection by Learning a Data-Driven Risk Score
families.path: Intent-assurance monitor. Learned risk and EMA thresholds raise drift alerts; SHAP and horizon rules supply attribution and time-to-failure ranges.
families.note: Risk scoring and time-series smoothing feed the alert decision.

families.title: MILD: Multi-Intent Learning and Disambiguation for Proactive Failure Prediction in Intent-based Networking
families.workflow: Multi-intent risk alerts and root-cause attribution
families.path: Multi-intent assurance monitor. Per-intent risk/gating selects alerts and root causes, with SHAP and horizon-based diagnostic outputs.
families.note: Primary evaluation uses labeled synthetic data, supplemented by a telemetry proof of concept.

families.title: Performance Comparison of IBN orchestration using LLM and SLMs
families.path: Intent workflow orchestrator; emulated-network controller. Junior agents propose topology/service choices; a senior generates code; a policy agent recommends OSPF/DUAL before deployment.

checks.Feasibility: A senior model compares proposals under policy constraints; emulation provides an instantiation failure signal.

families.title: Contract-based Agentic Intent Framework for Network Slicing in O-RAN
families.workflow: Intent contract to rApp policy and xApp control
families.path: Intent contract handler; SLA rApp; near-RT xApps. Agent translation becomes a TMF921 contract; an rApp prepares A1 policy; KPM-driven xApps calculate PRB ratios and execute E2 control.

checks.Feasibility: An evaluator agent checks extracted intent; the SLA rApp separately checks requested throughput against PRB/CQI performance history before generating A1 policy.

families.note: The SLA rApp estimates feasibility from performance history; numerical xApps act on current KPM data.

families.title: AI-driven Intent-Based Networking Approach for Self-configuration of Next Generation Networks
families.workflow: Policy activation; proposed ranked assurance repair
families.path: Intent handler; SDN activation; assurance (mixed implemented/proposed). Schema-constrained policy realization and conflict-aware activation are combined with predictive multi-intent assurance; ranked repair remains conceptual.
families.note: The thesis implements selected components; ranked repair and general conflict governance remain proposals.

families.title: NetAgentBench: A State-Centric Benchmark for Evaluating Agentic Network Configuration
families.workflow: Interactive routing commands to converged state
families.path: Network configuration/repair agent. Interactive FRR commands are evaluated against converged RIP/OSPF/BGP network state.
families.note: Evaluation scores converged network state after configuration actions.

families.title: A Reproducible Semantic Benchmark for Multivendor DSM-to-CLI Translation
families.workflow: Multivendor CLI generation and model judging
families.path: DSM-to-CLI translator; semantic evaluation layer. Models generate multivendor CLI; three model judges adjudicate semantic equivalence.

checks.Feasibility: A model-judge panel scores DSM/CLI semantic consistency during evaluation.

families.note: Judge agreement and token cost concern the benchmark evaluation pipeline.

families.title: Agentic AI-Based Joint Computing and Networking via Mixture of Experts and Large Language Models
families.path: Joint communications/computing optimizer. An LLM gate selects experts and constructs weights; learned expert outputs produce transmit/compute power and CPU allocations.
families.note: Continuous power and CPU allocations are constructed values.

families.title: Enhancing Secure Intent-Based Networking with an Agentic AI: The EU Project MARE Approach
families.workflow: Security intent completion to domain agents
families.path: Security intent handler; domain-agent orchestrator. The orchestrator checks intent support, fills missing parameters with the operator, plans action graphs, and invokes domain agents.

checks.Candidate coverage: Orchestrator classifies whether the system supports the intent and alerts the operator on unsupported requests.

families.title: Validated Intent Compilation for Constrained Routing in LEO Mega-Constellations
families.workflow: Offline intent compilation to certified LEO routing
families.path: LEO intent compiler; routing certifier/controller. Offline language compilation produces ConstraintProgram JSON; deterministic validation precedes constrained GNN routing.

checks.Feasibility: Eight-pass validator grounds entities and detects conflicts; supported fragments obtain constructive routing witnesses for simultaneous hard constraints.
checks.Candidate coverage: Certifier distinguishes ACCEPT, REJECT, and ABSTAIN; REJECT/acceptance guarantees are limited to supported fragments. Unsupported combinations use fallback without constructive certification.

families.note: ABSTAIN marks an unresolved certification outcome; feasibility and fallback success remain undetermined.

families.title: Benchmarking LLM-Driven Network Configuration Repair
families.path: Configuration diagnostic/repair assistant. Models select relevant files, locate routers, explain faults, and produce search/replace repairs in Cornetto.
families.note: Ground-truth forwarding checks score benchmark outputs.

families.title: TIO-SHACL: Comprehensive SHACL validation for TMF Intent Ontologies
families.path: Intent-ontology validator. TIO-SHACL returns conformance and violations for RDF intents and ontology functions.
families.note: Type, function-argument and hierarchy checks validate the intent representation.

families.title: Role-Based Agentic AI for Intent-Driven Network and Service Orchestration
families.workflow: Business intent to governed service orders
families.path: Business intent handler; supervisor; service orchestrator. Business RDF and governance-guided DAGs lead to OSL/OSM service orders; general resource agents remain architectural.

checks.Feasibility: MCP service tools are assigned feasibility/resource checks; supervisor governs admission, while the customer confirms semantic interpretation.

families.note: Evaluation measures the three-agent service-order workflow.

families.title: $E^3$-Agent: An Executable and Evolving Agent for Resource Management of Edge Generative Inference
families.workflow: Event-driven parameter updates to task routing
families.path: Event-driven meta-controller; edge task router. An LLM adjusts risk TTL/calibration/router parameters; deterministic fast-path scoring dispatches each task.

checks.Observation state: Performance model consumes only completed feedback available at the current timestamp; delayed/missing feedback leaves estimates unchanged until a valid record arrives.
checks.Candidate coverage: Router restricts to available devices, avoids risky ones if alternatives exist, and routes anyway with penalties when all are risky; admission/drop decisions belong to an outer policy.

families.title: AgentxGCore: Agentic AI for Next-Generation Mobile Core Network
families.path: Core-network orchestration agent. Plans create/remove UPFs and reassign users through SMF/PCF execution tools.

checks.Feasibility: The executor agent assesses plan feasibility before selecting execution tools.

families.note: The agent uses predictive telemetry and bounded context memory.

families.title: RAG-driven Multi-Agent LLM Framework with Task Decomposition for Beyond 5G Auto-Configuration
families.path: Configuration agent; gNB deployment orchestrator. Agents generate gNB configuration, return segmented review/repair reports, and prepare approved startup commands.

checks.Feasibility: A configuration-verification agent reviews generated segments and returns repair feedback; human approval gates startup commands.

families.title: Bridging High-Level Intent and Network Execution: Detecting Violations and Intent Drift Through Low-Level Traffic Analysis
families.workflow: Offline port-policy compliance and drift monitoring
families.path: Data-plane intent-assurance monitor. Port-policy rules flag violating flows; a fixed empirical baseline flags drift in offline traffic records.
families.note: Offline compliance experiments use a four-field projection of a conceptual seven-tuple.

families.title: Privacy-Preserving Intent Fulfilment and Assurance for 6G RAN
families.workflow: Intent profiles to O1 assurance counters
families.path: RAN management/assurance over O1. Intent categories map to resource profiles; aggregate performance counters determine fulfillment/degradation.
families.note: The O1 assurance interface uses aggregate performance counters.

families.title: Distilling Knowledge from Large Language Models into Lightweight Reinforcement Learning Agents for Autonomous Cyber Operations
families.path: Network defense policy. A language-model teacher and distilled PPO student choose network isolation/restoration actions in CybORG.
families.note: Teacher-guided action masking is applied during distillation.

families.title: Learning Not to Optimize: Physics-Informed Action-Space Reshaping for Intent-Based Network Control
families.path: Candidate-set guard; network deployment selector. Residual screening, symmetry quotienting, and dominance filtering form a frontier before action selection.

checks.Feasibility: Executor recomputes exact network-law residuals; invalid selected actions are rejected, repaired, or mapped to fallback.
checks.Candidate coverage: An empty executable set among generated candidates triggers fallback. The paper separates finite-generation coverage loss from screening correctness.

families.note: Screening certifies members of the generated candidate set.

families.title: NetConfArena: An Executable Benchmark for LLM Agents in Closed-Loop Network Configuration
families.workflow: Interactive CLI changes scored in emulation
families.path: Interactive network configuration agent. Agents produce and submit device CLI changes in an emulated network; task predicates score the resulting behavior.
families.note: Negative tests cover the benchmark's stated prohibitions.

families.title: Uncertainty Signals for Network Intent Translation: Risk Ranking and Ambiguity Localization
families.path: Intent translator; uncertainty-based review selector. Juniper command candidates are ranked by uncertainty for abstention/review; token entropy locates ambiguity.
families.note: Uncertainty scores determine candidate ranking and abstention.

families.title: On Identifying Adversarial Intent Injection in AI-Native 6G Networks
families.path: Intent security filter. A classifier marks an intent sequence window malicious when attack content is detected.
families.note: Evaluation uses synthetic attack-intent windows.

families.title: NetInspector: Measuring and Improving LLM Capabilities for Reliable Intent-Based Networking Policy Generation
families.workflow: Intent translation to tool-based policy inspection
families.path: Intent translator; policy-inspection agent. Entity prefiltering narrows policies; a tool-using agent queries network facts and returns Conflict or Safe.

checks.Observation state: A dedicated state manager versions and applies updates atomically so each query sees a consistent network snapshot.
checks.Feasibility: Deterministic tools resolve groups and query reachability, middleboxes, rule priorities, bandwidth, and temporal overlap; the LLM combines the replies into a terminal verdict.

families.note: Each query reads a consistent snapshot; the LLM assembles tool replies into the final verdict.

families.title: TelecomGPT-R1: Unified Post-Training for Reasoning Across Heterogeneous Telecom Tasks
families.path: Telecom diagnostic assistant. TeleLogs inputs produce a fault-class choice with supporting reasoning.
families.note: Rule/answer checks are used in training-data construction.

families.title: From Intents to Algorithms: Verified Algorithm Discovery for Transport Networks
families.workflow: Numerical algorithm search to path allocation
families.path: Intent compiler; transport algorithm search and allocator. Conceptual LLM/AST discovery is separated from measured numerical ranking-function evolution and deterministic path allocation.

checks.Feasibility: Trusted network functions retain capacity, latency, path-validity, and single-path feasibility; discovered algorithms rank alternatives without redefining those constraints.

families.note: Evaluation covers the ten-parameter numerical search; free algorithm generation remains proposed.

families.title: Intent2Tc: Automated Intent-to-Traffic Control Translation with Language Models
families.workflow: Intent compilation to corrected traffic-shaping rules
families.path: Traffic-shaping intent compiler. Language models produce metadata, declarative sub-intents, and Linux tc rules; deterministic correction intervenes between stages.

checks.Feasibility: A template-based correction module enforces scoped policy consistency and tc hierarchy, priority, filtering, and syntax constraints.

families.note: Template correction applies a fixed traffic semantic model.

families.title: Automatic Intent-Based Secure Service Creation Through a Multilayer SDN Network Orchestration
families.workflow: Multilayer SDN service setup and teardown
families.path: Multilayer SDN service orchestrator. Encryption/domain constraints select a layer and installation plan, followed by connection setup or teardown.
families.note: Encryption, path provisioning, installation acknowledgements, and teardown have separate responsibilities and timing endpoints.

families.title: Cross-stakeholder service orchestration for B5G through capability provisioning
families.path: Domain/capability/cross-domain service orchestrators (conceptual). Business goals map to domain configuration, capability/SLA instances, and end-to-end provider combinations.
families.note: The architecture specifies three functional transformations; decision-interface implementations are unspecified.

families.title: NetOrchLLM: Mastering Wireless Network Orchestration with Large Language Models
families.workflow: Wireless tool selection and allocation generation
families.path: Wireless model/tool orchestrator. Task/model selection and function calls support constructed bandwidth and multiuser power-allocation vectors.
families.note: Selecting a model/tool and constructing its numerical allocation output are distinct interfaces.

families.title: An Autonomous Network Orchestration Framework Integrating Large Language Models with Continual Reinforcement Learning
families.workflow: Semantic objectives to sequential resource actions
families.path: Network orchestration controller. Semantic objective/QoE decisions and user sequencing feed RL placement, capacity, and path allocation.

checks.Observation state: State history is updated after each user allocation before subsequent users are processed.
checks.Feasibility: Per-user/service state masking restricts the action executor to the represented feasible space.

families.note: The model constructs a user ordering and selects resource actions. Feasibility depends on the represented infrastructure and mask.

families.title: KP-A: A Unified Network Knowledge Plane for Catalyzing Agentic Network Intelligence
families.path: Network knowledge/query plane; edge-service agent. Live/static knowledge endpoints support state answers, service recommendations, and subscription creation.
families.note: The prototype demonstrates live queries; freshness and versioning are design requirements.

families.title: Agentic AI for SAGIN Resource Management_Semantic Awareness, Orchestration, and Optimization
families.workflow: Semantic rewards to RL placement/resource solving
families.path: SAGIN semantic manager; RL controller and resource solver. Semantic analysis shapes RL rewards; task placement/routing feeds continuous resource solving; command generation has a separate architectural scope.
families.note: Performance results cover the resource case study; command generation remains architectural.

families.title: WirelessBench: A Tolerance-Aware LLM Agent Benchmark for Wireless Network Intelligence
families.workflow: Tool-assisted wireless allocation and QoS decisions
families.path: Wireless allocation/feasibility assistant. Tool-augmented agents produce slice, CQI, bandwidth, throughput, mobility-conditioned allocation, and QoS decisions.

checks.Feasibility: The agent compares predicted throughput with a service minimum to produce the scoped QoS verdict; this remains part of the task being evaluated.

families.note: Benchmark scoring uses a tolerance criterion. Mobility/CQI dependency errors can propagate into the final QoS verdict.

families.title: Intent-Driven 6G Service Orchestration: Grounded Translation, Validation, and Decomposition
families.path: TMF-style intent/service-management boundary. Catalog discovery and RDF construction feed requirement extraction, minimum-cost CFSS choice, and RFSS coverage/decomposition.

checks.Feasibility: RequirementCapability predicates test all extracted requirements against profile capabilities; SHACL separately validates RDF structure.
checks.Candidate coverage: The capability layer determines whether any current catalog profile satisfies requirements; RFSS decomposition covers requirements using a greedy heuristic compared with CP-SAT.

families.note: Coverage is evaluated against supplied catalog profiles and requirement predicates.

families.title: MOSS: End-to-End Dialog System Framework with Modular Supervision
families.path: Network troubleshooting dialogue manager. Utterances update dialogue state, choose clarification/repair acts, and generate responses.
families.note: The network subset evaluates dialogue success in laptop-network troubleshooting.

families.title: MSADM: Large Language Model (LLM) Assisted End-to-End Network Health Management Based on Multi-Scale Semanticization
families.path: Network health/diagnosis assistant. Anomaly/fault classification and semantic state summaries support root-cause reports and tc mitigation suggestions.

checks.Feasibility: LLM prompts request evidence checks and constrained mitigation choices.

families.note: Mitigation outputs are suggested scripts.

families.title: LLMcap: Large Language Model for Unsupervised PCAP Failure Detection
families.path: Packet-trace diagnostic monitor. Masked-language-model reconstruction errors drive call-failure and frame/chunk localization decisions.
families.note: Generative reconstruction is an internal signal; the retained diagnostic outputs are detection/localization labels.

families.title: Adapting Network Information into Semantics for Generalizable and Plug-and-Play Multi-Scenario Network Diagnosis
families.path: Network knowledge and diagnostic assistant. Semantic/symbolic descriptions and KG updates support diagnosis plans, anomaly decisions, and explanatory reports.

checks.Feasibility: A Z3-assisted symbolic component reasons over represented network rules; the final diagnostic report remains a model output.

families.title: Leveraging Multi-Agent System (MAS) and Fine-Tuned Small Language Models (SLMs) for Automated Telecom Network Troubleshooting
families.workflow: Delegated telecom diagnosis and action planning
families.path: Telecom troubleshooting orchestrator. Coordinator and planner delegate diagnostic work, parameterize actions, and assemble root-cause reports.
families.note: Human approval gates executable plans; grounding and format checks also appear in training.

families.title: HYVE: Hybrid Views for LLM Context Engineering over Machine Data
families.path: Network troubleshooting assistant. Runbooks, anomaly identification, reports, API arguments, summaries, branch decisions, and test IDs use different output interfaces.
families.note: ValidateSourceCoverage checks preservation of serialized machine-data content.

families.title: Cross-Domain Query Translation for Network Troubleshooting: A Multi-Agent LLM Framework with Privacy Preservation and Self-Reflection
families.path: Cross-domain troubleshooting interface. Domain/intent classification and clarification precede anonymization, technical query translation, diagnosis, and user explanation.
families.note: Confidence scores trigger clarification; anonymization precedes diagnostic translation.

families.title: SADE: Symptom-Aware Diagnostic Escalation for LLM-Based Network Troubleshooting
families.workflow: Symptom probes to skill-based fault localization
families.path: Symptom-driven network diagnostic agent. Initial probes and deeper scans establish symptoms; a fault index routes to a skill that localizes a canonical fault/device.

checks.Observation state: The diagnostic workflow checks ambiguous reachability with direct-IP probes and inspects lower-layer evidence before accepting apparently healthy higher-layer observations.

families.note: The agent performs skill-based interpretation at runtime. Verified fault injection prepares the benchmark.

families.title: PropLLM: Propagation-Aware Scene Reconstruction for Network Fault Diagnosis
families.path: Propagation-aware network diagnostic model. Multimodal evidence produces a fault class and a generated root-cause/propagation chain.
families.note: Causal direction masks and timestamp biases constrain model reasoning.

families.title: Intent-Based Management of Next-Generation Networks: an LLM-Centric Approach
families.workflow: Multidomain intent translation to service descriptors
families.path: Multidomain/domain intent handlers; NFV/RAN orchestrators. Language decomposition and translation form NSD/RAND descriptors for domain activation.

checks.Feasibility: The architecture assigns structure, conflict, and predicted-resource feasibility checks to intent handlers before deployment.

families.note: Measured timing ends at descriptor translation. Validation mechanisms are proposed, and activation lies downstream.

families.title: Configtrans: Network Configuration Translation Based on Large Language Models and Constraint Solving
families.workflow: Parameter/command mapping to target CLI trees
families.path: Cross-vendor configuration translator. Constraint solving maps parameters; reranking/LLM choice selects commands and keywords; view ordering constructs the target CLI tree.

checks.Feasibility: CSP enforces command/parameter correspondence and consistent view structure within the translation problem.

families.title: Network CoPilot: Intent-Driven Network Configuration Updating for Service Guarantee
families.path: Network configuration-update assistant. A graph-enriched language model constructs OSPF/BGP parameter-update descriptions from intent, configuration, topology, and link state.

families.title: Intent-Based Management for Open RAN: Intelligent Network Configuration Automation via Chatbot
families.path: Chatbot intent handler; ONOS controller. Entity/intent extraction and dialogue acts produce NILE that is installed through REST or CLI.
families.note: ConflictResolver is planned for future implementation; the demonstrated path covers intent installation.

families.title: NetLLMBench: A Benchmark Framework for Large Language Models in Network Configuration Tasks
families.workflow: Command generation and probes in emulation
families.path: Network configuration benchmark agent. Models generate device-command JSON, request ping probes, and repair malformed responses.
families.note: Syntax verification and network-emulator feedback evaluate generated commands.

families.title: Towards LLM-Based Failure Localization in Production-Scale Networks
families.workflow: Production alert diagnosis with operator assistance
families.path: Production-network diagnostic copilot. Alert summaries and device anomalies/scores feed ranked root-cause explanations and operator-assisted incident localization.
families.note: Component timing, 24-hour API scopes, and operator-assisted resolution time are distinct evidence boundaries.

families.title: NetAssistant: Dialogue Based Network Diagnosis in Data Center Networks
families.path: Dialogue-based network diagnosis. Entity normalization and intent matching select workflows that produce network-health/root-cause reports for on-call users.
families.note: Workflow diagnosis and on-call resolution have different endpoints. Control/data-plane verification modules remain proposed.

families.title: Intent-Driven Network Management with Multi-Agent LLMs: The Confucius Framework
families.path: Network-management workflow/DSL assistant. Confucius plans DAG/MOP workflows, selects blocks, generates topology/query DSL, and coordinates diagnostic tools.

checks.Feasibility: Custom parsers, API/ORM dry runs, and graph-invariant validators provide task-specific feedback before use.

families.note: Retrieval filters stale documents; validators check specific DSL and network invariants.

families.title: Graph Structure-Enhanced Large Language Model for Optical Network Fault Diagnosis: An Explainable Alarm Root Cause Localization Approach
families.workflow: Alarm propagation graphs to root-cause diagnosis
families.path: Optical-network alarm diagnostic assistant. Models construct event topology/propagation matrices; adjacency construction and root-cause localization use the resulting graph.
families.note: The model constructs a structured matrix that supports graph-derived root-cause explanations.

families.title: LLM-Augmented Deep Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic O-RAN Network Slicing
families.workflow: LLM-assisted learning for O-RAN slice allocation
families.path: O-RAN slicing policy (LLM-augmented MARL). Critic-only and fuller LLM-assisted learning variants produce joint slice/UE resource-block allocation.
families.note: Training/critic assistance and per-action inference have separate evaluation scopes.

families.title: R-IBN: A reinforcement learning-based intent-driven framework for end-to-end service orchestration and optimization
families.workflow: Intent translation to learned service-chain placement
families.path: Intent handler; service-chain orchestrator. Language translation and contradiction classification feed GNN-assisted DRL SFC placement/routing.

checks.Feasibility: Embedding-similarity thresholds with KNN refinement flag intent-policy contradictions through a learned semantic check.

families.note: GNN state forecasts supply the input to placement and routing decisions.

families.title: CEGS: Configuration Example Generalizing Synthesizer
families.path: Configuration example retriever; formal synthesizer. Intent normalization/roles select examples and device mappings; templates are verified and symbolically completed.

checks.Feasibility: CEGS combines a Batfish-derived syntax parser, Python local attribute validation, NetComplete-based global verification, and formal template filling.

families.note: Formal correctness is relative to encoded intent, topology, and templates. Timing covers the complete synthesis.

families.title: Nissist: An Incident Mitigation Copilot based on Troubleshooting Guides
families.workflow: Clarified intent to guide-based mitigation actions
families.path: Incident mitigation copilot. Clarified intent selects troubleshooting-guide nodes and produces corrected diagnostic/mitigation actions.
families.note: The reviewed task is network connectivity; reported mitigation times aggregate mixed-cloud incidents.

families.title: A Holistic View of AI-driven Network Incident Management
families.path: Network incident-management assistant (conceptual). A proposed pipeline ranks hypotheses, plans tests and interprets monitors, then recommends mitigation.
families.note: The paper proposes module roles and future verification research.

families.title: Towards Explainable Network Intrusion Detection Using Large Language Models
families.path: Network intrusion detector and explanation layer. Llama/GPT variants classify flows and produce explanatory alerts in separate scopes.
families.note: The paper evaluates intrusion classification and explanations, and discusses inference limits for real-time detection.

families.title: FedLLMGuard: A Federated Large Language Model for Anomaly Detection in 5G Networks
families.path: 5G network anomaly detector. A federated, adapted language model classifies traffic/log embeddings as normal or anomalous.
families.note: Detection metrics have defined endpoints. The reported attack-mitigation time lacks an operational definition and leaves the mitigation path unspecified.

families.title: Can Jev Make SRE Agents More Reliable?
families.workflow: Agent diagnosis with ranked tests and evidence gates
families.path: SRE diagnosis/mitigation agent. The agent proposes hypotheses and read-only tests; Jev ranks the tests and reviews diagnosis and mitigation evidence; the agent runs tests and repairs.

checks.Observation state: jev_plan adds a fresh, bounded namespace snapshot before ranking; the diagnosis review requires evidence of a current application failure.
checks.Feasibility: Each mitigation-review question must reach probability 0.70, covering whether the repair addresses the cause, restored functionality, and appears durable. Rejection returns the agent to planning.

families.note: Jev ranks only agent-proposed tests; a missing hypothesis cannot be recovered by ranking. Pass rate is measured; time-to-diagnosis is not.

families.title: OrchestRAN: Network Automation through Orchestrated Intelligence in the Open RAN
families.workflow: Request-driven model placement and xApp dispatch
families.path: Non-RT RIC orchestrator (rApp); near-RT RIC/DU control apps. A BILP selects ML/AI Catalog models and nodes; containers are dispatched as xApps/dApps, and DRL agents select scheduling/slicing policies.

checks.Feasibility: Constraints enforce model performance, control-loop timescales, node resources, and connectivity to required input data; pruning removes infeasible model-node variables.
checks.Candidate coverage: A request is admitted only when deployed models provide all requested functionalities; the branching variant can accept requests on a subset of clusters.

families.note: Solver time comes from MATLAB/CPLEX simulation; the Colosseum prototype reports placement and network effects without orchestration timing.

families.title: Benchmarking Various ML Solutions in Complex Intent-Based Network Management Systems
families.path: Intent-based orchestrator for an ICT supply chain. An NLP intent manager emits JSON intents, a policy configurator matches stored policies, and an SVD/SGD recommender estimates ML-technique performance on devices.

checks.Feasibility: After configuring policies, the policy configurator checks conflicts before triggering the network controller; no implementation or evaluation is reported.
checks.Candidate coverage: The policy configurator checks whether the requested ML technique exists in the store and alerts the user when it does not; this check is described but not evaluated.

families.note: Evaluation covers recommender accuracy (normalized RMSE on AI-benchmark data); intent translation and policy configuration are architectural.

families.title: Bridging Language Models and Formal Methods for Intent-Driven Optical Network Design
families.workflow: Offline intent to planned optical network design
families.path: Optical network design assistant (pre-deployment). LLM grammar translation and optical RAG feed LLM-generated PDDL problems over a manual domain; an LLM agent translates the plan into a design.

checks.Feasibility: A Lark grammar parser validates structure and routes errors to automatic correction or user clarification; the PDDL solver plans under budget, latency, and protection constraints.
checks.Candidate coverage: When no plan satisfies the constraints, the solver reports infeasibility and the user receives feedback; the pipeline can fall back to disclosed LLM-only topology generation.

families.note: Case studies report 96.7% grammar-error detection, with 2 of 15 vague-value cases undetected. No deployed network state is measured.

families.title: BLINC: Context-Specific Causal Learning for Automated RAN Configuration
families.workflow: Offline causal priors to RAN power-control configuration
families.path: Non-RT RIC rApps with CI/CD deployment. LLM-derived mandatory/prohibited edges constrain Bayesian-network structure learning; inference scores P0/target-SNR configurations applied over O1/O2.

checks.Observation state: Recommendation scores each candidate configuration given current measurements; incremental CPD updates use new data, and a past recommendation degrades for cell-edge users.

families.note: LLM constraints keep edges voted by more than half of independent runs and enter the structure score. Recommendation searches a predefined feasible configuration space.

families.title: Proving the Utility of Large Language Models in Cybersecurity Simulations: A Comprehensive Examination
families.path: Cyber-simulation scenario generator. ChatGPT-4 generates YAML network configurations from templates or golden examples; validated scenarios feed LLM-synthesized Python attack agents.

checks.Feasibility: Topological checks cover adjacency, bidirectional firewall consistency, vulnerabilities, and process mappings; configurations that fail or do not run in NASim are discarded.

families.note: Generated attack agents print their own compromise verdict without an independent check. Validity rates combine schema, topology, and NASim outcomes.

families.title: Performance Evaluation of Intent-Based Networking Scenarios: A GitOps and Nephio Approach
families.path: GitOps reconcilers (Argo CD, Flux CD, ConfigSync) and the Nephio/Porch package orchestrator. Desired-state manifests pushed to Git are synchronized and deployed on Kubernetes; Nephio first hydrates intent packages.

checks.Observation state: Operators compare tracked desired states with runtime states and reconcile drift after webhook-detected pushes; ConfigSync synchronization reflects its polling period.

families.note: Intents are declarative manifests without language interpretation. The benchmark measures sync, deploy, and healthy times and resource use.
